transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-06-10 14:00 PT
- Duration: 55 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE) - Dr. Elena Morris (Quanta CTO), Mark Li (Quanta Head of ML), Sofia Ramos (Clinical ML Eng), Ben Carter (Infra)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on open-model shortlist and concrete success criteria for Quanta's clinical note extraction and summarization workload. Discussed throughput/latency targets, benchmark plan, timeline for a 4-week pilot, security/hosting options, and shortlist: Llama 2 Chat 70B variants, Mistral/Falcons 40B, and smaller Mistral 7B for latency experiments. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics:
- Success criteria: accuracy, hallucination rate, latency p95, cost per 1M tokens
- Workload sizing: avg tokens per request, peak QPS, daily volume
- Benchmarks: prompt set, labeled QA, hallucination measurement, structured output tests
- Timelines: 2-week baseline + 2-week focused test (4-week POC)
- Model shortlist & tradeoffs: Llama 2-Chat, Mistral 7B/8B, Falcon 40B; quantization vs fp16, RAG/fine-tune discussion
- Security & deployment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private

Action items (recap in call): see action_items field above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call and then we'll jump into scope - we had the intake form but want to confirm success criteria.
[00:12] Dr. Elena Morris: Hi, thanks. Yep. We're looking to evaluate models for clinical note extraction and condensed summaries for physicians. Key is precision on medication/diagnosis extraction, low hallucination, and sub-second-ish latency at tail during day ops.
[00:28] Mark Li: To add, we have multilingual notes - about 10% Spanish - and a bunch of domain-specific shorthand. So we need to test for multilingual capacity or a way to build a fallback for Spanish.
[00:42] Priya Desai: Got it. When you say sub-second at tail, can you quantify p95 or p99 SLOs?
[00:49] Dr. Elena Morris: p95 around 350 ms would be amazing, p99 under 700 ms. If that's impossible for larger models we'll consider a hybrid: smaller model for latency critical calls + larger for higher-fidelity async tasks.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Helpful. On volume - Ben, can you outline expected QPS and daily token volume?
[01:12] Ben Carter: Baseline 50 requests per minute during working hours, bursts to 300 rpm for specific shifts. Average request size probably 300 tokens in, 80 tokens out; roughly 5-7M tokens/day at baseline, peak maybe 20M tokens/day.
[01:29] Jordan Kim: Great, that helps sizing. For a POC we typically do constrained workload - 2 weeks to validate quality and a second 2-week for throughput/cost tuning. Does that align?
[01:38] Dr. Elena Morris: Yes. We want a 4-week POC with clear checkpoints.
[01:43] Priya Desai: For model shortlist, based on your constraints we recommend starting with: 1) Llama 2-Chat 70B (open weights variant) for quality baseline, 2) Mistral 7B or Mixtral (for lower-latency tests), 3) Falcon 40B Instruct as a mid-point. We'll try quantized fp8/fp4 variants on Redwood Dedicated for cost testing.
[02:05] Mark Li: Any thoughts about fine-tuning vs RAG? Our labeled data is limited, maybe a few thousand examples; we were thinking retrieval-augmented generation for entity precision.
[02:16] Priya Desai: That makes sense - if you only have a few thousand labeled examples, RAG plus lightweight prompt tuning or LoRA on a smaller model is often better for entity recall/precision without the full fine-tune lift. We'll set up a prompt + retrieval baseline first.
[02:29] Sofia Ramos: On hallucination metrics, what's the baseline we should aim for? < 5% hallucination for extracted fields?
[02:35] Jordan Kim: Customers typically set < 5% for critical fields like med lists/diagnosis. In the POC we'll measure hallucination via a labeled set and human review sampling.
[02:44] Dr. Elena Morris: Security wise, we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML/Okta), and controls around PHI. We may require VPC/private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
[02:56] Priya Desai: Redwood supports Hosted for fast iteration, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable performance, and Private VPC for tighter controls. For PHI we often recommend Dedicated with a customer KMS or Private deployment if air-gap is required. We can map your controls to our compliance matrix - we'll include that doc.
[03:12] Ben Carter: If we go Dedicated, are there network egress/firewall requirements from our side? We have an internal policy around approved IP ranges and peering.
[03:20] Liam O'Connor: We'll coordinate the network checklist - Ben we'll share our standard VPC peering and IP allowlist notes.
[03:27] Mark Li: Back to models - how do we handle multilingual? Do we pick a single model or route Spanish to a smaller Spanish-tuned model?
[03:36] Priya Desai: Two options: 1) pick a single multilingual model that handles both (some Llama variants and Falcon have reasonable Spanish), or 2) route non-English to an alternative model or translation pre-step. Because Spanish is only 10% I'd prototype with a multilingual model first and track error rates; if unacceptable we can route or augment retrieval with Spanish docs.
[03:56] Jordan Kim: For benchmarks we'll need: a) 50 representative prompts, b) 200 labeled examples for extraction precision recall (we can start with 50 and iterate), c) latency and cost harness. Priya will share the harness and a spreadsheet for results.
[04:12] Priya Desai: I'll share the benchmark template plus a small Redwood sample deck showing throughput/latency tradeoffs with quantization settings. Also linking a bench spreadsheet in chat.
[04:22] Dr. Elena Morris: On success criteria - let's list concrete pass/fail: 1) Extraction precision > 0.88 for meds and diagnoses, 2) Hallucination < 5% on critical fields, 3) p95 latency < 350 ms on the chosen latency-optimized stack, 4) Cost target under $300 per 1M tokens for production (we can be flexible for POC but want guidance).
[04:44] Jordan Kim: Noted. We'll include those as POC criteria and instrument the tests. Regarding cost, $300/1M is a reasonable target for our Hosted/Dedicated mix with quantized models; we'll run estimations and produce cost curves during the second week.
[04:58] Mark Li: How will caching or prefix caching impact cost? We have repeated headers and templates in notes.
[05:04] Priya Desai: Redwood has prefix and KV cache features; for structured extraction caching can reduce tokens significantly for repeated context. We'll suggest caching policies in the POC to reduce token usage - that'll be part of the Optimize playbook.
[05:17] Sofia Ramos: For the labeled examples we have some de-identified notes; any tips on formatting?
[05:22] Priya Desai: Prefer CSV with columns: raw_text, med_list, diagnosis_list, summary. If de-id is an issue, a synthetic subset is fine for initial tests.
[05:31] Jordan Kim: Timeline recap: Week 0 (this week) - exchange artifacts, benchmark template; Week 1-2 baseline quality runs on 3 model variants; Week 3-4 throughput/cost tuning and one focused security/integration test. Agree?
[05:44] Dr. Elena Morris: Agreed. We may need a security review earlier if the data must stay in our VPC. We can surface that by Monday.
[05:52] Liam O'Connor: We'll schedule a 30-min security runbook session for next week.
[05:56] Ben Carter: One more infra Q - what are the rollback/fallback patterns if Dedicated capacity is constrained in production?
[06:03] Priya Desai: Redwood supports policy-based routing and automatic fallback to hosted model variants. We can set up a policy: primary is Dedicated quantized 70B variant, fallback is a smaller 7B model or regional hosted endpoint. That keeps latency and availability predictable.
[06:18] Mark Li: Regarding evaluation metrics for hallucination, do you have tooling or heuristics we can reuse?
[06:24] Priya Desai: We'll provide a small evaluation harness that computes precision/recall, hallucination heuristics (insertion of extraneous entities), and a manual sample review workflow.
[06:33] Dr. Elena Morris: Good. On licensing - any constraints using Llama 2 weights for commercial use?
[06:39] Jordan Kim: Llama 2 has licensing requirements but is generally acceptable for production; we'll include notes and legal doc links. If you prefer fully permissive models we'll include alternatives.
[06:48] Sofia Ramos: For the RAG layer, what retrieval tech do you integrate with?
[06:52] Priya Desai: We can work with your existing vector DBs - we support Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, and more. If you don't have one we'll recommend a lightweight vector store for the POC.
[07:03] Dr. Elena Morris: OK. Anything else?
[07:06] Jordan Kim: Quick recap of deliverables and owners - see action items. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the security deep dive. Thanks all.
[07:14] Mark Li: Thanks everyone.

References shared in chat: link: https://redwood.ai/poc-benchmarks (Redwood benchmark template), link: https://s3.company/quanta-sample (placeholder for customer upload), pricing sheet placeholder: link: https://redwood.ai/pricing-dedicated
